title: Greece, Lithuania, Poland, Cyprus – Research and experimental development services – Pre-CommerciAl ProCuremenT of Innovative Personal ProtectiVe Equipment for First REsponders (ACTIVE PCP)
description: The Pre-CommerciAl ProCuremenT of Innovative Personal ProtectiVe Equipment for First REsponders (ACTIVE PCP) project addresses critical gaps in personal protective equipment (PPE). It responds to the need to keep first responders safe and operationally effective during evolving threats, from CBRN incidents and HAZMAT situations to terrorism, industrial accidents, natural disasters, and other complex emergencies. ACTIVE PCP involves public safety buyers and end-users in defining unmet needs and guiding industry R&D towards solutions. ACTIVE PCP procures R&D services through Pre-Commercial Procurement (PCP). // Tenderers are invited to propose innovative PPE solutions for first responders, police, firefighters, and emergency medical services operating in complex CBRN and HAZMAT environments. Following the phased PCP model, the procurement supports R&D up to the development of a limited volume of first products. It comprises 3 competitive Phases, with fewer Tenderers progressing at each stage so that those offering the strongest response to the PCP's technical challenge are selected. // The PCP will be implemented by means of a Framework Agreement (FA) with call-offs for specific contracts for each of the 3 R&D phases (altogether ‘Contracts’). description: The 414th Contracting Support Brigade (RCO Italy) intends to issue a competitive Request for Quotation (RFQ) for professional, non-personal Core Environmental Compliance Support Services at the Darby Military Community (DMC) in Pisa/Livorno, Italy. The Contractor shall act as an independent environmental compliance consultant, providing specialized services to support the environmental engineering and compliance program for the Directorate of Public Works (DPW) Environmental Division (ED). The core tasks are structured under the following seven (7) functional areas: Environmental Plan Administration: Review, update, and maintain environmental media management plans (including Drinking Water, Storm Water, Solid Waste, Spill Response, and Asbestos) IAW the Italian Final Governing Standards (IFGS). Bilingual Training & Spill Exercises: Coordinate and conduct Hazardous Waste Handler (HWH) and Hazardous Material Handler (HMH) classroom training sessions and mock spill response exercises in both English and Italian. Compliance Inspections: Conduct monthly compliance assessments of Hazardous Waste Accumulation Points (HWAPs), motor pools, and aboveground/underground storage tanks, and annual inspections of air and wastewater assets. Database Management: Input and maintain environmental quality tracking data in standard military administrative systems (WEBCASS, SWAR Web, and Installation Status Reports). Host-Nation Permitting Support: Prepare technical engineering documentation to support permit requests and renewals with regional Italian authorities in accordance with Italian Legislative Decree D.Lgs. 152/06. title: Cost Effective On-Base Parcel Delivery Solutions (RAFL, RAFM, RAFF, United Kingdom)
description: The 48th Contracting Squadron at Royal Air Force (RAF) Lakenheath, United Kingdom, seeks to identify qualified sources and cost-effective commercially practical solutions capable of providing reliable on-base parcel delivery services for RAF Lakenheath (RAFL), RAF Mildenhall (RAFM), and RAF Feltwell (RAFF) in the United Kingdom. Purpose of Market Research: Our primary objective is to gain an understanding of how the Government's required delivery outcome can be achieved at a reasonable/sustainable cost while also being reliable. The Government is not seeking an unnecessarily complex or premium delivery model where a simpler commercial solution could reliably satisfy the requirement. *This RFI is issued solely for market research and acquisition planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quote (RFQ), or promise to issue a future solicitation. Responses are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs associated with preparation or submission of information in response to this RFI. * Background: Personnel who live or work on RAFL, RAFM, and RAF Feltwell receive both personal and official parcels from commercial delivery companies. The most common carriers, presently, have been DPD, DHL, Evri, FedEx, Parcelforce, UPS, Amazon, and Royal Mail. Royal Mail/Parcelforce are the only delivery entities that presently have installation access and deliver directly to the on-base addresses. Other commercial parcel delivery companies do not have installation access, creating challenges in completing delivery to the intended on-base residence or agency. The Government is exploring a recurring parcel delivery service capable of receiving or otherwise obtaining parcels from commercial carriers that do not have installation access and completing final delivery to the intended residence or agency on RAF Lakenheath, RAF Mildenhall, or RAF Feltwell. The Government seeks industry�s recommendations regarding the most efficient and economical means of accomplishing this outcome. Packages, after they are picked up by a neighbor, have an average dwell time of 2 weeks before the intended recipients of the packages become aware that a neighbor had received their package on their behalf. The Government is particularly interested in solutions that make use of existing commercial capabilities and minimize unnecessary Government-specific processes, facilities, equipment, or infrastructure. Primary Constraints: Installation access and funding will be the primary constraints and will be the biggest factors considered in developing the desired solution. Presently installation access for local nationals can take upwards of 7 months due to the MOD clearance/background check process. The government is not aware of any route to expedite the processing of packages. It has been observed that the delivery driver experiences a high level of turnover, unpredictable routes for drivers, and criminal records that prohibit access to the installation which affects the parcel delivery companies� ability to obtain installation access for their drivers. Drones are not permitted on or near these installations and should not be included in identified solutions. Government-provided escorts will not be available as an interim staffing or access solution. Respondents should consider these conditions when describing their proposed solution and should identify how they could achieve the required staffing and access capability within the anticipated transition period. Respondents should also identify cost-effective approaches for maintaining sufficient access-qualified staffing without unnecessarily increasing the number of personnel requiring installation access. Estimated Parcel Volume: Available information indicates that approximately 1,000 parcels per week are associated with RAF Lakenheath that are being coordinated for pick-up at businesses near the installation. Should a reliable delivery service be established, the volume of parcels is expected to at least triple. Comparable parcel-volume information is not currently available for RAFM or RAFF. The bases in order of highest estimated volume to lowest are as follows: RAFL, RAFF, RAFM. All quantities provided in this RFI are estimates for market research and planning purposes and should not be interpreted as guaranteed quantities or maximum quantities. Suggested solutions will need to be scalable to fluctuate as personnel to the bases fluctuate and parcel volume fluctuates. Respondents should identify how uncertainty and fluctuations in parcel volume would affect their recommended solution and pricing. Respondents are also encouraged to suggest a Contract Line Item Number (CLIN) structure best suited to their recommendation. Respondents are specifically encouraged to identify approaches that allow the service to scale efficiently as parcel volume changes without requiring the Government to pay for unnecessary excess capacity during lower-volume periods. Desired Outcome: The desired outcome is a reliable and cost-effective service capable of delivering eligible parcels from commercial delivery companies that do not have installation access to the residence or agency on the installation that ordered the item. The service would be expected to support RAFL, RAFM, and RAFF. All three installations are anticipated to be included from the very beginning of performance. The service would handle both personal and official parcels. Delivery service is expected seven days per week. For residential deliveries, parcels that do not require a recipient signature may be left at the recipient's door (or in a safe place designated by their delivery notes). The Government recognizes that commercial carriers may transfer parcels at different times throughout the day. Respondents should identify any operational assumptions, carrier coordination, cutoff times, or other conditions necessary to accomplish daily delivery. Solutions should not be disruptive, so the preference is to find a solution to deliver packages by 1700 each day ensuring no nighttime disruptions. If a requirement or assumption described in this RFI would have a significant impact on the cost, please identify the cost driver and recommend a less expensive alternative that would still provide reliable on-base parcel delivery. The Government is interested in understanding how industry could establish effective and economical means of accepting, collecting, transferring, consolidating, or otherwise obtaining custody of eligible parcels from commercial delivery companies and subsequently completing final delivery to the appropriate on-base residence or agency. The Government has not determined whether an on-base facility, off-base facility, consolidation point, direct carrier transfer, existing commercial facility, existing delivery network, or another method represents the most effective solution. title: Technology Licensing Opportunity: Room-Temperature Electrochemical Metallization of Rare Earth Elements
description: Note: This is a technology licensing opportunity. No procurement, grants, or funding opportunities are associated with this notice. Room-Temperature Electrochemical Metallization of Rare Earth Elements A low-energy, low-hazard alternative to molten-salt electrolysis for sustainable REE production. Technology Summary This invention introduces a method to produce metallic rare earth elements (REEs) through room-temperature electrometallization in anhydrous electrolytes. By leveraging unique ion-pairing interactions, Lewis acid-base chemistry, and interfacial structuring, the system enables efficient REE reduction and stable metal formation without the extreme energy use or toxic byproducts of conventional fused salt electrolysis. Problem Addressed High cost & regulatory barriers: Current molten-salt electrolysis (600�1200 �C) generates toxic HF gas and rare earth fluoride waste, triggering costly EPA and OSHA compliance requirements. Environmental impact: Legacy processes produce hazardous waste with long-term contamination risks, leading to industry abandonment in North America. Supply chain dependence: Metallic REEs are only produced at scale in China, creating vulnerabilities for U.S. manufacturers and defense applications. Solution The invention replaces high-temperature fused salt electrolysis with an ambient-temperature electrochemical process. The approach integrates three synergistic innovations: Tuned electrolyte nucleophilicity � enabling more efficient reduction pathways. Lewis acid-base coordination control � stabilizing the ligand environment during deposition. Interfacial electrochemical structuring � improving reaction kinetics and metal stability. This combination allows REE electrodeposition at room temperature, reducing both energy demand and hazardous byproduct formation. This invention enables dual functionality, electrodeposition and (in-situ) electrorefining. Key Advantages Lower energy consumption � eliminates the need for 600�1200 �C molten salt processes. Reduced environmental liabilities � avoids HF gas emissions and toxic fluoride salt accumulation. Safer operations � circumvents EPA and RCRA compliance barriers tied to FSE. Domestic supply potential � enables North American REE production for critical industries. Scalable platform � adaptable to multiple REEs including neodymium, samarium, dysprosium, and terbium. Market Applications Permanent magnets � essential for EV traction motors, wind turbines, and energy-efficient refrigeration. Defense systems � critical components for satellites, communication devices, and advanced weapons. Lightweight alloys � enhancing aerospace and automotive materials. Electronics � miniaturized devices requiring REE-based components. Battery technologies � advanced REE-containing chemistries for high-performance storage.

The Government is considering several compliant acquisition pathways to ensure the successful delivery of this complex Design-Build project in Peru. All interested firms are strongly encouraged to submit a comprehensive capabilities statement, as the information received will be critical in determining the final method of procurement. The primary anticipated strategy is a Two-Phase Design-Build procurement under the authority of FAR Part 36.3. In this scenario, the Government would issue a public Phase 1 solicitation requesting offeror qualifications. title: Henkilöstön osaamisen kehittämisen palvelut 2027-2029 (2030)
description: Henkilöstön osaamisen kehittämisen palvelut 2027-2029 (2030) Hankinnan kohteena on Jyväskylän kaupungin henkilöstöön kuuluvien esimiesten ja työyhteisöjen osaamisen kehittämisen palvelut. Hankintaa ei ole jaettu osiin, sillä jakaminen ei palvelun luonteen vuoksi ole tarkoituksenmukaista eikä jaosta saada selkeää. Sen sijaan poolista tehdään melko suuri, jotta saadaan laaja-alainen asiantuntijuus turvattua. Palveluiden hankinta voidaan toteuttaa joko henkilöstöhallinnon tai työyksiköiden esimiesten hankkimana tilanteissa, joissa on havaittu kehittämistarvetta. Tuleva hankinta koskee kaikkia Jyväskylän kaupungin toimialoja ja liikelaitoksia. Tarjouskilpailulla muodostetaan 15 yrityksen/toimijan pooli, tai useamman, mikäli mukaan ei saada vähintään 25 valmentajaa. Jos soveltuvia tarjouksia on vähemmän kuin 15, valitaan kaikki soveltuvat tarjoukset. Jotta turvataan pientenkin toimijoiden pääseminen hankintaan mukaan, rinnakkaisia tarjouksia ei hyväksytä, ja yksi yritys/toimija voi tarjota 1-3 asiantuntijaa pooliin. Palvelun käynnistämisen tavoiteaika on 1.3.2027. Lisätiedot hankinnan kohteesta tarjouspyynnöstä ja sen liitteistä.,

title: Vartiointi- ja hälytyskeskuspalvelut
description: Vartiointi- ja hälytyskeskuspalvelut Hankinnan kohteena on vartiointi- ja hälytyskeskuspalvelut Kainuun hyvinvointialueella. Palvelun kohteena ovat Tilaajan Toimeksiantosopimuksissa määrittelemät kohteet. Turvallisuuspalvelut sisältävät paikallisvartiointia, kiertävä vartiointi (ent. piirivartiointi), hälytys- ja tilausvartiointia. Vartiointipalveluiden tarkoituksena on ylläpitää ja edistää turvallisuutta sovituilla vartioimisalueilla ja -kohteissa, sekä tarvittaessa ryhtyä lain (Laki yksityisistä turvallisuuspalveluista 1085/2015) sallimissa rajoissa toimenpiteisiin turvallisuuden palauttamiseksi. Vartiointi - ja hälytyskeskuspalvelu koostuu mm. seuraavista palveluista (tarkemmin kuvattu Palvelukuvauksessa (liite 6): -Paikallisvartiointi; siihen liittyvä tilausvartiointi (yksittäinen tehtävä etukäteen tilattu) -Hälytyskäynnit -Kiertävä vartiointi (ent. piirivartiointi) -Hälytyskeskuspalvelu (esim. murtohälytysjärjestelmien testaus/hälytyksen siirrot, hälytysten vastaanottaminen) -Henkilöturvaan, omaisuuteen ja kiinteistöön liittyvät hälytykset Kainuun hyvinvointialueen toimitiloissa ja kiinteistöissä (mm. ovien kiinniolojen seuranta, jääkaappihälytykset, N-kaappien hälytykset, henkilöstön avustaminen pukukaappien avauksessa) -Yleiset kiinteistön pitoon liittyvät aputyöt (esim. puku- ja laukkukaappien avaukset vikatilanteessa, tarvittaessa pukukaappien tarkastukset), Vuototilanteissa huolto/kalustesulkujen sulkeminen (päivystävä huoltomies ohjeistaa), lipunnosto Kainuun keskussairaalassa -Aula- ja paikallisvartiointipalvelut Kainuun keskussairaalassa: (esim. väliaikaisten kulkuoikeuksien ja - lupien hallinta, palohälytyksiin reagointi ja keskussairaalan kuulutukset) Hälytyskeskuspalvelut sisältyvät toimeksiantosopimukseen ilman erillistä korvausta palvelukuvauksen mukaisesti. Hälytyskeskuspalvelun tarkoituksena on jatkuva päivystäminen (24/7 palvelu), joka mahdollistaa erilaisten palvelupyyntöjen vastaanottamisen ja niihin reagoimisen.,

title: Finland – Public road transport services – Reittipohjaiset joukkoliikennepalvelut, brutto, tarjouskilpailu 2026-15
description: Liikenne- ja viestintävirasto Traficom (jäljempänä Traficom) pyytää tarjousta joukkoliikennepalvelujen hoitamisesta ajalla 7.6.2027-2.6.2030 reitillä Mynämäki-Nousiainen-Masku-Turku (tarkempi kohdemäärittely tarjouspyynnön liitteessä). Sopimus sisältää option sopimuksen jatkamisesta ajalle 3.6.2030 - 5.6.2033. Tarkat liikennöinnin aloitus ja lopetuspäivät määräytyvät kouluvuoden mukaisesti. Liikenne hankitaan bruttosopimuksella. Bruttosopimuksella tarkoitetaan palvelusopimusasetuksen (1370 /2007) ja erityisalojen hankintalain (1398/2016) tarkoittamaa joukkoliikenteen palvelusopimusta, jossa lipputuloriski on liikenteen tilaajalla. Tämän hankinnan sisältämälle liikenteelle myönnetään palvelusopimusasetuksen mukainen yksinoikeus erillisellä hallinnollisella päätöksellä. Yksinoikeuspäätöksessä otetaan huomioon mahdollinen reitin osan läpi kulkeva pidempimatkainen liikenne. Lippu- ja maksujärjestelmävaatimukset sekä liikennepalvelulain (320/2017) edellyttämät yhteentoimivuusvaatimukset on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnössä ja sen liitteissä. Maskun, Mynämäen ja Nousiaisten kunnat osallistuvat kohteen rahoitukseen.

title: Finland – Real estate services – Syväkeräysastioiden vuosihuollot / VAV
description: Tilaajan tavoitteena on hankkia joustava ja luotettava yhteistyökumppani Vantaalla sijaitsevien VAV-konsernin omistamien vuokratalokohteiden syväkeräysjätepisteiden vuosihuoltoihin. VAV-konserni omistaa noin 12 000 vuokra-asuntoa, joissa asuu noin 19 000 asukasta. Tarkempi luettelo sopimuksen piiriin kuuluvista syväkeräyskohteista on tarjouspyynnön liitteenä olevassa kohdeluettelossa. Sopimus ei sisällä määräostovelvoitetta, eikä Tilaaja sitoudu tarjouspyynnössä tai hankintailmoituksessa esitettyihin arvioihin hankintamääristä. Työtilauksiin voi sisältyä myös tarvikehankintoja ja muita työn suorittamiseen liittyviä palveluhankintoja. Tavoitteiden saavuttamisen edellytykset on kerrottu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön ESPD-lomakkeella, hankinnan kohteen kriteerit -osiossa sekä hankintailmoituksen liitteissä. Hankintapäätöksen tekoperusteena on kokonaistaloudellinen edullisuus pisteytyksen mukaisesti, jossa maksimipisteet ovat 1000 pistettä. Tarjoajan on annettava tarjous kaikista tarjouslomakkeen töistä. Mikäli Tarjoaja ei ole tarjonnut kaikkia tarjouslomakkeeseen eriteltyjä töitä, tulkitaan tarjous puutteelliseksi. Puutteellinen tarjous hylätään. Tarjoajan kannalta huomioitavaa on myös se, että tarjottujen töiden ja hintojen tulee sisältää kaikki tässä tarjouspyynnössä, hankintasopimusluonnoksessa ja palvelukuvauksessa määritellyt kriteerit. Palvelu toteutetaan tarjouspyynnön, palvelukuvauksen ja laatuvaatimusten mukaisesti. Tarjoajan antama tarjous on sitova. Hankintasopimus syntyy vasta kirjallisen sopimuksen allekirjoittamisella, selonottoneuvottelujen jälkeen. EU-kynnysarvon ylittävässä hankinnassa sopimus voidaan tehdä aikaisintaan 14 vuorokauden kuluttua siitä, kun Tarjoaja on saanut tai hänen katsotaan saaneen päätöksen perusteluineen tiedoksi. Tarjoaja ei saa esittää esimerkiksi omissa tarjousasiakirjoissaan ehtoja, jotka vaikuttaisivat hankintasopimuksen sisältöön. Sopimuskauden tavoitealkamisajankohta on 1.2.2027 ja sopimus on voimassa toistaiseksi, kuuden (6) kuukauden irtisanomisajalla.

title: Evaluering- Operativt SaLTo
description: Bydel Alna har behov for ekstern bistand til evaluering av prosjektet Operativt SaLTo. Prosjektet dreier seg om å finne nye metoder for å motvirke og forebygge ungdomskriminalitet. Evalueringen skal gi et faglig og operativt beslutningsgrunnlag for videreutvikling, videreføring og eventuell implementering av prosjektets samarbeidsmodell og arbeidsmetodikk. Oppdraget skal belyse hvordan modellen fungerer i praksis, identifisere hvilke deler som bør videreføres, justeres eller avsluttes, og vurdere organisatoriske forutsetninger for videreføring. Et særskilt formål er å vurdere hvordan erfaringer, metoder og arbeidsformer fra prosjektet kan tas i bruk i ny organisasjon etter bydelsreform fra 2028. Estimert verdi på anskaffelsen er 700 000 kroner ekskl. mva.

title: Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) Modeling & Simulation Support
description: This Request for Information (RFI) is being issued by the Department of the Army, on behalf of Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Fires. This solicitation is for the procurement of maintenance, repair and modernization of non-nuclear surface ships (including Guided-Missile Cruisers (CGs), Guided Missile Destroyers (DDGs), Expeditionary Sea Bases (ESBs), Guided-Missile Frigates (FFGs), Amphibious Command Ships (LCCs), Littoral Combat Ships (LCSs), Landing Helicopter Assaults (LHAs), Landing Helicopter Docks (LHDs), Landing Platform Docks (LPDs), Landing Ship Docks (LSDs), and Mine Countermeasures Ships (MCMs) homeported in or visiting the Norfolk region. PAEM intends to award IDIQ-MACs based on the qualifications and capabilities of the Contractor in the following two categories: MAC A, where all holders can complete all requirements; and MAC B, where all holders can complete work associated with CMAVs and EM on non-critical systems. MAC A will be solicited on a full and open basis. MAC B will be solicited as a Small Business Set Aide. MAC A � CMAV/EM includes work on critical systems. MAC A also includes short-term CNO availabilities. Due to the nature of critical systems and the likelihood of urgent requirements with critical EM, the Government will require contractors with the capability and capacity to respond immediately to critical technical requirements. It is anticipated that this work would be available under full and open competition. However, if it is determined that two or more small businesses are interested and capable of completing the scope of work under any given delivery order, contracting officers may use their discretion to restrict competition to small businesses. MAC B � CMAV/EM does not include work on critical systems but will include systems and equipment requiring work certification. The scope of non-critical contract actions is expected to require less contractor capabilities, both in human resources and facilities. MAC B will be a small business set aside. In the event that there is no interest expressed for any given delivery order, this work may be competed under MAC A. Offerors must possess or have the ability to obtain a Tier I, II, or III Master Ship Repair Agreement (MSRA) for the Norfolk, VA homeport. Each contract will include five (5) one-year ordering periods. The supply being procured is the repaired, mission ready vessel, which is returned to service within the Fleet. The solicitation will be issued electronically via System for Award Management (SAM) at http://sam.gov and interested parties must comply with that announcement. Interested offerors should monitor the SAM.gov page for any applicable amendments to this solicitation. Offerors must be registered in the System for Award Management in order to participate in this procurement at https://www.sam.gov/portal/public/SAM/. All responsible sources may submit a proposal in response to the solicitation, which shall be considered by the agency. SAM.gov is the single point of entry for posting of the synopsis and solicitations to the internet. This pre-solicitation notice is for information purposes only and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government to solicit contractual offers or award of contracts. The Government is not soliciting, nor will it accept, proposals as a result of this synopsis. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any questions submitted or information provided as a result of this notice. The solicitation is forthcoming.

title: Germany – Miscellaneous general and special-purpose machinery – Planung, Dimensionierung und Installation einer Abluftreinigung für den Biocampus MultiPilot (BMP)
description: Der ZVH schreibt die Planung, Lieferung, Montage, Inbetriebnahme und betriebsfertige Übergabe einer Abluftreinigung aus. Gereinigt werden sollen zwei Abluftströmen aus dem Prozessbereich. AXX aus ATEX-Bereichen mit ca. 1.020 Nm³/h sowie AEX aus übrigen Prozessbereichen mit ca. 3.300 Nm³/h. Aufgrund des diskontinuierlichen BMP-Betriebs sind schwankende Abluftbelastungen zu berücksichtigen. Die Grenzwerte der TA Luft für organische Stoffe und Ammoniak sind einzuhalten. Die Planung berücksichtigt zudem die Sicherstellung der natürlichen Belichtung der Aula, die Nutzung der neuen Dachflächen für Photovoltaik sowie die weitere Ausarbeitung des Brandschutzkonzepts. • Zu vergebende Leistungen: Stufenweise Beauftragung der Leistungsphasen 2 anteilig und 3 - 9; Objektplanung gem. §34 HOAI 2021

The USCG Station at Cape Disappointment requires repairs, upgrades, and improvements to existing infrastructure and nearby areas to restore and retain full mission readiness. The Station is on an unstable sandbar which has experienced sediment migration into dock and adjacent waterway areas. Dock structures are failing and require repair/replacement. The vessel haul-out facility is currently inoperable due to sedimentation and requires the USCG to conduct frequent maintenance dredging. Haul-out structure is failing and requires replacement. Adjacent landscape features pose rockfall dangers above the engineering and maintenance buildings to people and property 3. Project Scope. Rockfall slope instability corrective measures: Anticipated rockfall mitigation will require corrective measures including but not limited to tree removal, rock scaling, rock dowel installation, draped mesh removal and replacement, removal and/or repair of an existing damaged ringnet fence, and installation of a midslope attenuator system. Rockfall mitigation will require difficult access techniques to reach the full height of the hazardous slope. Temporary protection of the facility and workers will be required. Repairs to damaged roadways, utilities or access pathways may be required. Repair of an existing small landslide slump along the access road is required. Final mitigation work will reduce rockfall risk to USCG personnel and facility. Waterfront structures and vessel haul-out: The waterfront structures require repairs and upgrades. Replacement of the existing floating docks is required; they will retain their current configuration (footprint) but utilize updated material specifications. Existing timber and steel piles will be either replaced, or reused with new floats, as part of this contract, depending on current condition. Geotechnical, civil, structural, mechanical, and electrical scope is included. Constraints include: Float A to be retained; guide piles at floating docks #2 and #4 to be replaced; wave screens to be replaced; electrical equipment to be upgraded; existing vessel haul-out facility to be replaced. Eel grass and SAV surveys are required to inform design. Dock operations are to be maintained during construction, per phasing to be outlined by the government. The design will utilize modern, resilient coastal engineering practices including Nature-Based Solutions (NBS), dynamic revetments, segmented offshore breakwaters/sills, and the beneficial reuse of dredged sediment wherever practicable. Construction may be implemented in functional phases to optimize funding and operational readiness. Shoreline protection repairs and upgrades are considered part of this category along with the Haul Out structure. Interim repair work: Interim repair work may be required on existing structures before new design and construction activity can be completed. If the need arises, USACE will provide USCG a description of the recommended repairs and a cost estimate.
